newsitem.title: USA: Russian emigre in L.A. charged in Cosby murder.
newsitem.headline: Russian emigre in L.A. charged in Cosby murder.

text.p: An 18-year-old Russian emigre has been charged with murdering the only son of entertainer Bill Cosby, Los Angeles police chief Willie Williams said Thursday.
He told reporters the man, Mikhail Markhasev, had been born in the former Soviet Union but had lived in the United States for eight years.

There was no indication that the killing of Ennis Cosby was connected to any Russian organised crime group as some reports had suggested. "Even though he is of Russian origin, there are no indications that there is any Russian Mafia gang or any Russian Mafia tie at all," Williams said
Williams also said that race did not appear to have played a part in the killing. Markhasev is white, Cosby was black.
Cosby, 27, was gunned down in the early hours of Jan. 16 while changing a tire on his luxury Mercedes car by the side of a freeway.
"It appears that robbery was the motive; it was happenstance," said Williams, suggesting it was a random crime rather than a planned attack.

The police chief told the news conference that the murder weapon had been recovered "in an open area of Los Angeles" along with a knit cap after a tip-off from the National Enquirer tabloid. Forensic tests showed the gun had fired the fatal shot.
The suspect was charged with one count of murder, said the police chief. Markhasev, who closely resembled the composite sketch of the suspected killer, has not yet been arraigned.
Two other people who were questioned by police have been released, he said.
